content.content:
1	"""Write-ahead log key value store.
2	
3	Every mutation is first appended to a framed log. A commit marker is the
4	only thing that advances the durable sequence number. When a store is opened,
5	any tail that was never committed (including a record torn by a hard kill) is
6	discarded, so recovery always yields exactly the committed state.
7	
8	Only the very last log record may be incomplete: a process killed while
9	appending leaves at most one torn record, which is dropped without being
10	applied. Any other framing failure -- a truncated record in the middle, a
11	length field out of bounds, unparseable content, or a duplicate/regressing
12	commit sequence -- is corruption, and recovery raises ``CorruptLogError``
13	without touching the store.
14	
15	Recovery itself may be killed at any point, any number of times. Two small
16	sidecar files in the store directory, both maintained below the write path,
17	make the convergence protocol kill-safe and its report stable:
18	
19	``wal.ckp``
20	    A byte-for-byte copy of the log prefix ending at the most recent commit
21	    marker, replaced atomically (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync)
22	    only after that commit frame is durable. A log torn at *any* offset --
23	    even offset 0, or inside the committed prefix -- is rebuilt from it, so
24	    the durable sequence number never regresses. It is also the published
25	    snapshot read-only processes pin (see below).
26	
27	``wal.rec``
28	    A recovery marker written only after a log needing repair has passed
29	    full validation and only *before* the atomic rebuild starts. It records
30	    the clean prefix length and whether a torn record was discarded. Its
31	    presence makes a rebuild interrupted mid-copy converge on reopen (the
32	    rebuild is simply repeated) and keeps the reported ``discarded`` count
33	    stable across reopens and repeated recoveries. It is removed by the next
34	    successful commit.
35	
36	Read-only processes (``Store(path, read_only=True)``) take no lock and never
37	create or modify a file. At open each one picks the highest committed prefix
38	available at that instant -- the validated ``wal.log`` prefix or ``wal.ckp``
39	-- scans it once into memory and serves every ``get`` from that index.
40	Because the chosen image is complete and is only ever replaced atomically
41	(never edited in place), a refresh caught mid-rename, a half-written commit,
42	a torn record, or a log being rebuilt or shrunk can never expose partial
43	bytes: each read lands on one full committed snapshot that was current at or
44	after the open. A directory written by an older version is opened the same
45	way from its log and checkpoint. Reads never replay the log afterwards, so
46	their cost is independent of history and they never block the writer; a
47	reader that is killed or simply hangs changes nothing on disk.
48	
49	The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log boundary,
50	the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can never move
51	backwards. Every repair step is either idempotent or an atomic rename; a
52	kill between any two steps leaves a state the next open converges from to
53	the identical result.
54	
55	Log frame layout (all integers big-endian)::
56	
57	    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+
58	    | b"WAL2" | payload_length | header_crc | payload              | crc32   |
59	    | 4 bytes | 8 bytes        | 4 bytes    | metadata\\n<value>    | 4 bytes |
60	    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+
61	
62	``header_crc`` is the crc32 of the magic and length bytes. It makes a
63	partial header that borrows bytes from a following frame fail validation,
64	so an incomplete record in the middle of the log reads as corruption while
65	a genuinely short final header reads as a torn tail.
66	
67	Metadata is a compact JSON object: ``{"t":"p","k":key}`` for puts,
68	``{"t":"d","k":key}`` for deletes and ``{"t":"c","s":seq}`` for commits.
69	The raw value bytes follow the first newline, so values need no encoding.
70	"""
71	
72	from __future__ import annotations
73	
74	import json
75	import os
76	import sys
77	import zlib
78	
79	__all__ = ["Store", "CorruptLogError", "inject_tear"]
80	
81	
82	class CorruptLogError(ValueError):
83	    """The write-ahead log is corrupt, not merely missing a torn tail.
84	
85	    A single incomplete final record is a normal crash remnant and is
86	    discarded during recovery. Anything else that fails framing, checksum,
87	    metadata or commit-sequence validation is corruption; recovery stops
88	    without applying or removing anything.
89	    """
90	
91	
92	LOG_NAME = "wal.log"
93	_CHECKPOINT_NAME = "wal.ckp"
94	_MARKER_NAME = "wal.rec"
95	
96	_MAGIC = b"WAL2"
97	_PREFIX = 12  # 4 bytes magic + 8 bytes payload length
98	_HEADER = 16   # prefix + 4 bytes crc32 of the prefix
99	_TRAILER = 4   # crc32 of the payload
100	_MAX_PAYLOAD = 1 << 40
101	
102	_OP_PUT = "p"
103	_OP_DELETE = "d"
104	_OP_COMMIT = "c"
105	
106	
107	def _encode_frame(op: str, value: bytes = b"", key: str | None = None,
108	                  seq: int | None = None) -> bytes:
109	    meta: dict[str, object] = {"t": op}
110	    if key is not None:
111	        meta["k"] = key
112	    if seq is not None:
113	        meta["s"] = seq
114	    head = json.dumps(meta, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
115	    payload = head + b"\n" + value
116	    prefix = _MAGIC + len(payload).to_bytes(8, "big")
117	    header = prefix + zlib.crc32(prefix).to_bytes(4, "big")
118	    return header + payload + zlib.crc32(payload).to_bytes(4, "big")
119	
120	
121	def _iter_frames(f):
122	    """Scan an open binary log file from position 0.
123	
124	    For every intact frame yields
125	    ``("frame", meta, value, start, end)``. Scanning stops with either no
126	    terminal event (clean EOF), ``("torn", start)`` for a single incomplete
127	    final frame, or ``("invalid", start)`` for a frame that fails framing,
128	    header/payload checksum or metadata parsing. With the header checksum a
129	    partial header that borrows bytes from a following record cannot survive,
130	    so a short read landing exactly at EOF is reliably the one unfinished
131	    record a single writer was appending when it died; bytes left beyond such
132	    a read instead make it corruption.
133	    """
134	    f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
135	    eof = f.tell()
136	    f.seek(0)
137	    while True:
138	        start = f.tell()
139	        header = f.read(_HEADER)
140	        if not header:
141	            return
142	        if len(header) < _HEADER:
143	            # Trailing bytes of a frame header are a torn tail only when
144	            # nothing follows them; a gap anywhere else is corruption.
145	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
146	                   else ("invalid", start))
147	            return
148	        if header[:4] != _MAGIC:
149	            yield "invalid", start
150	            return
151	        if int.from_bytes(header[_PREFIX:], "big") != zlib.crc32(
152	                header[:_PREFIX]):
153	            yield "invalid", start
154	            return
155	        length = int.from_bytes(header[4:_PREFIX], "big")
156	        if length > _MAX_PAYLOAD:
157	            yield "invalid", start
158	            return
159	        payload = f.read(length)
160	        checksum = f.read(_TRAILER)
161	        if len(payload) < length or len(checksum) < _TRAILER:
162	            # Only the single final record may be incomplete.
163	            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
164	                   else ("invalid", start))
165	            return
166	        if int.from_bytes(checksum, "big") != zlib.crc32(payload):
167	            yield "invalid", start
168	            return
169	        newline = payload.find(b"\n")
170	        if newline < 0:
171	            yield "invalid", start
172	            return
173	        try:
174	            meta = json.loads(payload[:newline])
175	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
176	            yield "invalid", start
177	            return
178	        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not isinstance(meta.get("t"), str):
179	            yield "invalid", start
180	            return
181	        yield "frame", meta, payload[newline + 1:], start, f.tell()
182	
183	
184	def _fsync_dir(path: str) -> None:
185	    """Fsync a directory so a nearby rename/unlink is durable.
186	
187	    Windows cannot open directories for fsync and raises ``PermissionError``
188	    (access denied); directory entries there are made durable by the file's
189	    own flush-on-rename, so skipping the directory fsync keeps store creation
190	    working everywhere.
191	    """
192	    if sys.platform == "win32":
193	        return
194	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
195	    try:
196	        try:
197	            os.fsync(fd)
198	        except PermissionError:
199	            # Some non-Windows mounts reject directory fsync the same way.
200	            pass
201	    finally:
202	        os.close(fd)
203	
204	
205	def _write_all(fd: int, data: bytes) -> None:
206	    view = memoryview(data)
207	    while view:
208	        view = view[os.write(fd, view):]
209	
210	
211	def inject_tear(source, destination, offset):
212	    """Copy a log cut at exactly ``offset`` bytes, for bytewise verification.
213	
214	    Produces ``destination`` containing the first ``offset`` bytes of
215	    ``source`` -- a replica of a process killed precisely when the write had
216	    reached that byte offset. The source file is never modified. Either path
217	    argument may be a store directory, in which case its ``wal.log`` is used.
218	
219	    ``offset`` must satisfy ``0 <= offset <= len(source)``; a negative or
220	    past-the-end offset raises ``IndexError``. The full-length copy
221	    (``offset == len(source)``) is the clean control case.
222	
223	    Verification aid only; the normal write path never calls this.
224	    """
225	    if not isinstance(offset, int) or isinstance(offset, bool):
226	        raise TypeError("offset must be an integer byte offset")
227	
228	    src = os.path.join(source, LOG_NAME) if os.path.isdir(source) else source
229	    dst = (os.path.join(destination, LOG_NAME)
230	           if os.path.isdir(destination) else destination)
231	
232	    size = os.path.getsize(src)
233	    if offset < 0 or offset > size:
234	        raise IndexError(
235	            f"tear offset {offset} out of range for log of {size} bytes")
236	    if os.path.abspath(src) == os.path.abspath(dst):
237	        raise ValueError("tear destination must differ from the source log")
238	
239	    remaining = offset
240	    with open(src, "rb") as fsrc, open(dst, "wb") as fdst:
241	        while remaining:
242	            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
243	            if not chunk:  # pragma: no cover - size came from the same file
244	                raise IndexError("source log shrank while copying")
245	            fdst.write(chunk)
246	            remaining -= len(chunk)
247	        fdst.truncate(offset)
248	        os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
249	    return dst
250	
251	
252	class Store:
253	    """A single-writer key value store backed by an append-only log.
254	
255	    ``path`` must be an existing store directory; the log file inside it is
256	    created on first use. Opening a missing directory raises
257	    ``FileNotFoundError`` and opening a path that is not a directory raises
258	    ``OSError``.
259	
260	    With ``read_only=True`` the store is opened purely for reading. No file
261	    is ever created or modified, and no lock is taken: any number of
262	    read-only processes may coexist with the one writer. The reader pins the
263	    committed snapshot current at open time -- the highest committed prefix
264	    of ``wal.log`` or of the atomically replaced ``wal.ckp`` sidecar --
265	    scans it once, and serves every ``get`` from that in-memory index. The
266	    snapshot is independent of the log's later history, so a read never
267	    replays the log and cannot block the writer, and uncommitted bytes, a
268	    half-written commit, a torn record or a half-finished rebuild are never
269	    visible. ``put``, ``delete``, ``commit`` and ``recover`` are rejected on
270	    a read-only store; ``stats`` reports the pinned snapshot.
271	    """
272	
273	    def __init__(self, path: str, read_only: bool = False):
274	        self._dir = path
275	        self._path = os.path.join(path, LOG_NAME)
276	        self._ckp_path = os.path.join(path, _CHECKPOINT_NAME)
277	        self._marker_path = os.path.join(path, _MARKER_NAME)
278	        self._read_only = read_only
279	
280	        # Recovery needs a directory to replay; a missing target is an error
281	        # at open time, not an implicit create.
282	        if not os.path.exists(path):
283	            raise FileNotFoundError(
284	                f"store directory does not exist: {path!r}")
285	        if not os.path.isdir(path):
286	            raise OSError(f"store path is not a directory: {path!r}")
287	
288	        self._data: dict[str, bytes] = {}
289	        self._seq = 0
290	        self._entries = 0
291	        self._pending = 0
292	        self._closed = False
293	        self._corrupt = False
294	        # Torn records dropped in this recovery epoch; wal.rec carries it
295	        # across processes until the next commit.
296	        self._discarded = 0
297	
298	        if read_only:
299	            # A read-only open holds no writable fd and never takes a lock;
300	            # leave the writer fd slot unset for clarity.
301	            self._fd = -1
302	            self._open_read_only()
303	            return
304	
305	        log_created = not os.path.exists(self._path)
306	        self._fd = os.open(self._path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND,
307	                           0o644)
308	        if log_created:
309	            os.fsync(self._fd)
310	            _fsync_dir(path)
311	
312	        self._converge_on_open()

314	    # -- log scanning and validation --------------------------------------
315	
316	    def _read_log(self, path=None):
317	        frames = []
318	        terminal = None
319	        with open(path or self._path, "rb") as f:
320	            for event in _iter_frames(f):
321	                if event[0] == "frame":
322	                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
323	                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
324	                else:
325	                    terminal = event
326	        return frames, terminal

328	    @staticmethod
329	    def _validate(frames, terminal):
330	        """Validate every frame and the strictly increasing commit sequence.
331	
332	        Returns ``(committed_end, last_seq)`` -- the byte offset just past
333	        the last commit marker and its sequence number. An ``"invalid"``
334	        terminal is corruption and raises ``CorruptLogError``; a ``"torn"``
335	        terminal is left for the caller, which decides from the durable
336	        checkpoint whether it is a tail to discard or a gash to restore.
337	        """
338	        expected_seq = 1
339	        last_seq = 0
340	        committed_end = 0
341	        for meta, _value, _start, end in frames:
342	            op = meta.get("t")
343	            if op in (_OP_PUT, _OP_DELETE):
344	                key = meta.get("k")
345	                if not isinstance(key, str) or key == "":
346	                    raise CorruptLogError(
347	                        f"invalid frame metadata: {meta!r}")
348	            elif op == _OP_COMMIT:
349	                seq = meta.get("s")
350	                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
351	                    raise CorruptLogError(
352	                        f"invalid commit marker: {meta!r}")
353	                if seq != expected_seq:
354	                    raise CorruptLogError(
355	                        f"commit sequence {seq} out of order, "
356	                        f"expected {expected_seq}")
357	                last_seq = seq
358	                expected_seq += 1
359	                committed_end = end
360	            else:
361	                raise CorruptLogError(f"unknown frame type: {op!r}")
362	        if terminal is not None and terminal[0] == "invalid":
363	            raise CorruptLogError("corrupt log frame")
364	        return committed_end, last_seq
365	
366	    @staticmethod
367	    def _replay(frames) -> tuple[dict[str, bytes], int]:
368	        state: dict[str, bytes] = {}
369	        applied = 0
370	        for meta, value, _start, _end in frames:
371	            op = meta["t"]
372	            if op == _OP_COMMIT:
373	                continue
374	            if op == _OP_PUT:
375	                state[meta["k"]] = value
376	            else:  # _OP_DELETE
377	                state.pop(meta["k"], None)
378	            applied += 1
379	        return state, applied

381	    # -- crash-convergence sidecars ---------------------------------------
382	
383	    @staticmethod
384	    def _copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, length: int) -> None:
385	        remaining = length
386	        while remaining:
387	            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
388	            if not chunk:
389	                raise CorruptLogError(
390	                    "source ended before the committed prefix")
391	            fdst.write(chunk)
392	            remaining -= len(chunk)
393	        fdst.truncate(length)

395	    def _atomic_file(self, target: str, write) -> None:
396	        """Replace ``target`` atomically: temp file, fsync, rename, dir fsync."""
397	        tmp = target + ".tmp"
398	        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
399	            write(f)
400	            os.fsync(f.fileno())
401	        os.replace(tmp, target)
402	        _fsync_dir(self._dir)
403	
404	    def _write_checkpoint(self, end: int) -> None:
405	        """Persist the log prefix ``[0, end)`` as the clean checkpoint."""
406	        if end <= 0:
407	            return
408	
409	        def write(fdst):
410	            with open(self._path, "rb") as fsrc:
411	                self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, end)
412	
413	        self._atomic_file(self._ckp_path, write)
414	
415	    def _checkpoint_boundary(self) -> int:
416	        """Commit boundary the durable checkpoint covers; 0 if absent.
417	
418	        A checkpoint that is torn, unparseable or not exactly one committed
419	        prefix is corruption of the recovery machinery rather than a discard.
420	        """
421	        try:
422	            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._ckp_path)
423	        except FileNotFoundError:
424	            return 0
425	        if not frames:
426	            # An empty checkpoint covers the empty prefix; anything non-empty
427	            # that parses to no frames is corruption.
428	            if os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path) == 0 and terminal is None:
429	                return 0
430	            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint is not a clean committed prefix")
431	        if terminal is not None:
432	            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint is not a clean committed prefix")
433	        end, _seq = self._validate(frames, None)
434	        if end != os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path):
435	            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint has bytes past its commit")
436	        return end

438	    def _write_marker(self, clean_end: int, discarded: int) -> None:
439	        payload = json.dumps(
440	            {"end": clean_end, "discarded": discarded},
441	            separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
442	
443	        def write(f):
444	            f.write(payload)
445	
446	        self._atomic_file(self._marker_path, write)
447	
448	    def _read_marker(self):
449	        try:
450	            with open(self._marker_path, "rb") as f:
451	                raw = f.read()
452	        except FileNotFoundError:
453	            return None
454	        try:
455	            marker = json.loads(raw)
456	            end = marker["end"]
457	            discarded = marker["discarded"]
458	        except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):
459	            raise CorruptLogError("unparseable recovery marker")
460	        if (not isinstance(end, int) or isinstance(end, bool) or end < 0
461	                or discarded not in (0, 1)):
462	            raise CorruptLogError("invalid recovery marker")
463	        return end, discarded
464	
465	    def _remove_marker(self) -> None:
466	        try:
467	            os.unlink(self._marker_path)
468	        except FileNotFoundError:
469	            return
470	        _fsync_dir(self._dir)
471	
472	    def _remove_stale_temps(self) -> None:
473	        for name in (self._path + ".tmp", self._ckp_path + ".tmp",
474	                     self._marker_path + ".tmp"):
475	            try:
476	                os.unlink(name)
477	            except FileNotFoundError:
478	                pass
479	
480	    def _rebuild_log(self, clean_end: int) -> None:
481	        """Make the log exactly its clean ``[0, clean_end)`` prefix.
482	
483	        Kill-safe and idempotent: when a checkpoint covers the prefix the new
484	        log is fully written and fsynced as a temp file and atomically renamed
485	        over the old one, so a kill leaves either the old log or the complete
486	        restored log -- never a half-written file -- and rerunning converges.
487	        Without a checkpoint but with the committed bytes still at stable
488	        offsets, a synced truncate drops the tail instead. The empty prefix is
489	        a truncate to zero.
490	        """
491	        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
492	        if size == clean_end:
493	            return
494	
495	        if clean_end == 0:
496	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
497	            os.fsync(self._fd)
498	            return
499	
500	        try:
501	            ckp_size = os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path)
502	        except FileNotFoundError:
503	            ckp_size = -1
504	
505	        if ckp_size < clean_end and size > clean_end:
506	            # No checkpoint, but the committed bytes survive at stable
507	            # offsets: drop the dirty tail. Idempotent if killed mid-call.
508	            try:
509	                os.fsync(self._fd)
510	            except OSError:
511	                pass
512	            os.ftruncate(self._fd, clean_end)
513	            os.fsync(self._fd)
514	            return
515	        if ckp_size < clean_end:
516	            raise CorruptLogError(
517	                "committed prefix is torn and no checkpoint covers it")
518	
519	        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
520	        with open(self._ckp_path, "rb") as fsrc, open(tmp, "wb") as fdst:
521	            self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, clean_end)
522	            os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
523	        # Windows cannot rename over a path held open by the append fd.
524	        os.close(self._fd)
525	        try:
526	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
527	            _fsync_dir(self._dir)
528	        finally:
529	            self._fd = os.open(
530	                self._path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
531	        if os.fstat(self._fd).st_size != clean_end:
532	            raise CorruptLogError("restore did not converge")
533	
534	    def _converge(self):
535	        """Validate and converge the on-disk log to its clean state.
536	
537	        Returns ``(frames, discarded)`` for the now-clean log. Raises
538	        ``CorruptLogError`` without changing anything if the log is corrupt.
539	        Safe to run repeatedly and safe to kill at any point.
540	
541	        The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log
542	        boundary, the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can
543	        never regress. A log torn inside its committed prefix is rebuilt from
544	        the checkpoint and ``discarded`` stays 0 (those bytes were committed,
545	        not an unfinished write); a torn or merely uncommitted tail past the
546	        boundary is discarded, and the marker freezes that report until the
547	        next commit even when the kill lands mid-repair.
548	        """
549	        self._remove_stale_temps()
550	        marker = self._read_marker()
551	        marker_end = -1
552	        marker_discarded = 0
553	        if marker is not None:
554	            marker_end, marker_discarded = marker
555	
556	        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
557	        log_end, _log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
558	        ckp_end = self._checkpoint_boundary()
559	        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
560	
561	        target = max(log_end, ckp_end, marker_end)
562	        # The target bytes must come from somewhere still on disk: the
563	        # validated log itself or the checkpoint.
564	        if target > log_end and target > ckp_end:
565	            raise CorruptLogError("recovery target has no durable source")
566	
567	        log_clean = terminal is None and size == log_end
568	
569	        if log_clean and log_end == target:
570	            # Nothing to repair. An old marker whose epoch a newer commit
571	            # closed durably can finally go; otherwise its discarded count
572	            # stays frozen until that commit.
573	            if marker is not None:
574	                if target > marker_end:
575	                    self._remove_marker()
576	                    discarded = 0
577	                else:
578	                    discarded = marker_discarded
579	            else:
580	                discarded = 0
581	            if ckp_end < target:
582	                self._write_checkpoint(target)
583	            return frames, discarded
584	
585	        if target > log_end:
586	            # Committed bytes were torn away (offset 0 included): the
587	            # checkpoint is the source of truth. The discarded count is only
588	            # meaningful when the marker pins this exact boundary.
589	            discarded = marker_discarded if target == marker_end else 0
590	            self._rebuild_log(target)
591	        else:
592	            # A dirty suffix sits past the boundary. Decide discarded from
593	            # the suffix itself: a torn final record counts, complete
594	            # uncommitted frames do not. This also covers a repair killed
595	            # before the rebuild (the original suffix is still here, so the
596	            # same decision is reached) and fresh writes appended after a
597	            # previous repair (a new crash is a new decision rather than the
598	            # old marker's). A marker is only frozen once the log itself is
599	            # rebuilt clean; see the clean branch above.
600	            discarded = 1 if terminal is not None else 0
601	            if ckp_end < target:
602	                # Make the prefix independently restorable before we publish
603	                # the plan or remove any bytes.
604	                self._write_checkpoint(target)
605	            self._write_marker(target, discarded)
606	            self._rebuild_log(target)
607	
608	        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
609	        end, _seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
610	        if end != target or terminal is not None:
611	            raise CorruptLogError("restore did not converge")
612	        return frames, discarded
613	
614	    def _publish(self, frames, discarded) -> None:
615	        state, _applied = self._replay(frames)
616	        self._data = state
617	        self._seq = max(
618	            (meta["s"] for meta, _v, _s, _e in frames
619	             if meta.get("t") == _OP_COMMIT),
620	            default=0)
621	        self._entries = len(frames)
622	        self._pending = 0
623	        self._discarded = discarded
624	        self._corrupt = False
625	
626	    def _converge_on_open(self) -> None:
627	        """Crash cleanup at open; leave a corrupt store inert for recover()."""
628	        try:
629	            frames, discarded = self._converge()
630	        except CorruptLogError:
631	            self._corrupt = True
632	            return
633	        self._publish(frames, discarded)

635	    # -- read-only opens --------------------------------------------------
636	
637	    def _open_read_only(self) -> None:
638	        """Pin a committed snapshot without creating or modifying anything.
639	
640	        No lock is taken and nothing on disk is written. The reader chooses
641	        the highest committed prefix available at the instant it opens --
642	        the validated prefix of ``wal.log`` or the existing ``wal.ckp``
643	        sidecar, which the writer replaces atomically as part of every
644	        commit -- scans that prefix once into memory, and serves every
645	        ``get`` from that index. Later reads are independent of log history,
646	        never replay the log and never block the writer.
647	
648	        The checkpoint is a complete, self-contained image that is never
649	        modified in place (only atomically replaced), so reading it cannot
650	        expose uncommitted bytes, a half-written commit, a torn record or a
651	        half-finished rebuild/shrink. It is also what makes the pin safe once
652	        the reader closes the file: the image survives any later rename.
653	        """
654	        frames, end, seq = self._choose_readonly_prefix()
655	        state, _applied = self._replay(frames)
656	        self._ro_index: dict[str, bytes] = state
657	        self._ro_seq = seq
658	        self._ro_entries = len(frames)
659	        self._ro_bytes = end
660	
661	    def _choose_readonly_prefix(self):
662	        """Return ``(frames, end, seq)`` for the highest committed snapshot.
663	
664	        Takes the higher of the validated log boundary and the checkpoint
665	        boundary, mirroring the writer's durable-boundary rule. A torn or
666	        merely uncommitted tail past the last commit is excluded; a framing
667	        or sequence failure in committed bytes is corruption and raises
668	        ``CorruptLogError``. The checkpoint is the source when a crash or a
669	        concurrent rebuild has torn/shrunk the committed log bytes.
670	        """
671	        log_frames = None
672	        log_end = -1
673	        log_seq = 0
674	        if os.path.exists(self._path):
675	            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._path)
676	            log_end, log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
677	            # Keep only frames at or before the last commit; the torn final
678	            # record already arrives as the terminal, not as a frame.
679	            log_frames = [fr for fr in frames if fr[3] <= log_end]
680	
681	        ckp = self._read_clean_prefix(self._ckp_path)
682	        if ckp is None:
683	            if log_frames is None:
684	                return [], 0, 0
685	            return log_frames, log_end, log_seq
686	
687	        ckp_frames, ckp_end, ckp_seq = ckp
688	        if log_end >= ckp_end:
689	            return log_frames, log_end, log_seq
690	        return ckp_frames, ckp_end, ckp_seq
691	
692	    def _read_clean_prefix(self, path: str):
693	        """Validate ``path`` as an exact committed prefix.
694	
695	        Returns ``(frames, end, seq)`` or ``None`` if the file is absent.
696	        Raises ``CorruptLogError`` when it exists but is not exactly a clean
697	        committed prefix: such a sidecar is replaced atomically, so a torn
698	        or unparseable image cannot be a publish caught mid-flight. The size
699	        used for the "bytes past its commit" check is taken from the same
700	        open inode that was scanned, so a concurrent atomic replace can
701	        never mix the bytes of one version with the size of another.
702	        """
703	        try:
704	            f = open(path, "rb")
705	        except FileNotFoundError:
706	            return None
707	        with f:
708	            frames = []
709	            terminal = None
710	            for event in _iter_frames(f):
711	                if event[0] == "frame":
712	                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
713	                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
714	                else:
715	                    terminal = event
716	            size = os.fstat(f.fileno()).st_size
717	        if terminal is not None:
718	            raise CorruptLogError("sidecar is not a clean committed prefix")
719	        if not frames:
720	            if size == 0:
721	                return frames, 0, 0
722	            raise CorruptLogError("sidecar is not a clean committed prefix")
723	        end, seq = self._validate(frames, None)
724	        if end != size:
725	            raise CorruptLogError("sidecar has bytes past its commit")
726	        return frames, end, seq

728	    def _read_key(self, key: str) -> bytes | None:
729	        value = self._ro_index.get(key)
730	        return None if value is None else bytes(value)

732	    # -- argument validation ----------------------------------------------
733	
734	    @staticmethod
735	    def _check_key(key) -> None:
736	        if not isinstance(key, str):
737	            raise TypeError("key must be a string")
738	        if key == "":
739	            raise ValueError("key must not be empty")
740	
741	    def _ensure_open(self) -> None:
742	        if self._closed:
743	            raise ValueError("store is closed")
744	
745	    def _ensure_writable(self) -> None:
746	        self._ensure_open()
747	        if self._read_only:
748	            raise ValueError("store is opened read-only")
749	        if self._corrupt:
750	            raise CorruptLogError(
751	                "log is corrupt; call recover() to diagnose before writing")
752	
753	    # -- public API --------------------------------------------------------
754	
755	    def put(self, key: str, value: bytes) -> None:
756	        self._ensure_writable()
757	        self._check_key(key)
758	        if not isinstance(value, bytes):
759	            raise TypeError("value must be bytes")
760	        _write_all(self._fd, _encode_frame(_OP_PUT, value=value, key=key))
761	        self._data[key] = value
762	        self._pending += 1
763	        self._entries += 1
764	
765	    def get(self, key: str) -> bytes | None:
766	        self._ensure_open()
767	        self._check_key(key)
768	        if self._read_only:
769	            return self._read_key(key)
770	        return self._data.get(key)
771	
772	    def delete(self, key: str) -> None:
773	        self._ensure_writable()
774	        self._check_key(key)
775	        _write_all(self._fd, _encode_frame(_OP_DELETE, key=key))
776	        self._data.pop(key, None)
777	        self._pending += 1
778	        self._entries += 1
779	
780	    def commit(self) -> int:
781	        self._ensure_writable()
782	        if self._pending == 0:
783	            return self._seq
784	        _write_all(self._fd, _encode_frame(_OP_COMMIT, seq=self._seq + 1))
785	        os.fsync(self._fd)
786	
787	        # The commit frame is durable first, so even a kill here leaves a
788	        # clean log the next open refreshes the checkpoint from. Publish the
789	        # new restorable prefix, then close the recovery epoch.
790	        clean_end = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
791	        self._write_checkpoint(clean_end)
792	        had_marker = os.path.exists(self._marker_path)
793	        self._seq += 1
794	        self._pending = 0
795	        self._entries += 1
796	        self._discarded = 0
797	        if had_marker:
798	            self._remove_marker()
799	        return self._seq
800	
801	    def recover(self) -> dict:
802	        """Replay the log and return ``{"applied", "discarded", "seq"}``.
803	
804	        ``applied`` counts the committed put/delete records replayed,
805	        ``discarded`` is 1 when a single torn final record was dropped (0
806	        otherwise) and ``seq`` is the durable sequence number after recovery.
807	        Raises ``CorruptLogError`` (a ``ValueError``) if the log is corrupt;
808	        nothing is applied or truncated in that case.
809	
810	        Recovery is idempotent and kill-safe: interrupting it any number of
811	        times and rerunning converges to the same state and the same report
812	        as one clean recovery, and the next commit always uses ``seq + 1``.
813	        """
814	        self._ensure_open()
815	        if self._read_only:
816	            raise ValueError("cannot recover a store opened read-only")
817	        if self._pending:
818	            raise ValueError(
819	                "cannot recover with uncommitted changes in this session")
820	
821	        # Re-validate and re-converge; a genuinely corrupt log raises here
822	        # before anything is applied or removed.
823	        frames, discarded = self._converge()
824	
825	        state, applied = self._replay(frames)
826	        seq = max(
827	            (meta["s"] for meta, _v, _s, _e in frames
828	             if meta.get("t") == _OP_COMMIT),
829	            default=0)
830	        self._data = state
831	        self._seq = seq
832	        self._entries = len(frames)
833	        self._pending = 0
834	        self._discarded = discarded
835	        self._corrupt = False
836	        return {"applied": applied, "discarded": discarded, "seq": seq}
837	
838	    def stats(self) -> dict:
839	        self._ensure_open()
840	        if self._read_only:
841	            # The pinned snapshot's sequence, frame count and byte size; it
842	            # does not move as the writer appends later history.
843	            return {
844	                "seq": self._ro_seq,
845	                "entries": self._ro_entries,
846	                "bytes": self._ro_bytes,
847	            }
848	        return {
849	            "seq": self._seq,
850	            "entries": self._entries,
851	            "bytes": os.fstat(self._fd).st_size,
852	        }
853	
854	    def close(self) -> None:
855	        if self._closed:
856	            return
857	        if not self._read_only:
858	            os.close(self._fd)
859	        self._closed = True
860	
861	    def __enter__(self) -> "Store":
862	        return self
863	
864	    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
865	        self.close()

"""Write-ahead log key value store.

Every mutation is first appended to a framed log. A commit marker is the
only thing that advances the durable sequence number. When a store is opened,
any tail that was never committed (including a record torn by a hard kill) is
discarded, so recovery always yields exactly the committed state.

Only the very last log record may be incomplete: a process killed while
appending leaves at most one torn record, which is dropped without being
applied. Any other framing failure -- a truncated record in the middle, a
length field out of bounds, unparseable content, or a duplicate/regressing
commit sequence -- is corruption, and recovery raises ``CorruptLogError``
without touching the store.

Recovery itself may be killed at any point, any number of times. Two small
sidecar files in the store directory, both maintained below the write path,
make the convergence protocol kill-safe and its report stable:

``wal.ckp``
    A byte-for-byte copy of the log prefix ending at the most recent commit
    marker, replaced atomically (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync)
    only after that commit frame is durable. A log torn at *any* offset --
    even offset 0, or inside the committed prefix -- is rebuilt from it, so
    the durable sequence number never regresses. It is also the published
    snapshot read-only processes pin (see below).

``wal.rec``
    A recovery marker written only after a log needing repair has passed
    full validation and only *before* the atomic rebuild starts. It records
    the clean prefix length and whether a torn record was discarded. Its
    presence makes a rebuild interrupted mid-copy converge on reopen (the
    rebuild is simply repeated) and keeps the reported ``discarded`` count
    stable across reopens and repeated recoveries. It is removed by the next
    successful commit.

Read-only processes (``Store(path, read_only=True)``) take no lock and never
create or modify a file. At open each one picks the highest committed prefix
available at that instant -- the validated ``wal.log`` prefix or ``wal.ckp``
-- scans it once into memory and serves every ``get`` from that index.
Because the chosen image is complete and is only ever replaced atomically
(never edited in place), a refresh caught mid-rename, a half-written commit,
a torn record, or a log being rebuilt or shrunk can never expose partial
bytes: each read lands on one full committed snapshot that was current at or
after the open. A directory written by an older version is opened the same
way from its log and checkpoint. Reads never replay the log afterwards, so
their cost is independent of history and they never block the writer; a
reader that is killed or simply hangs changes nothing on disk.

The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log boundary,
the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can never move
backwards. Every repair step is either idempotent or an atomic rename; a
kill between any two steps leaves a state the next open converges from to
the identical result.

Log frame layout (all integers big-endian)::

    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+
    | b"WAL2" | payload_length | header_crc | payload              | crc32   |
    | 4 bytes | 8 bytes        | 4 bytes    | metadata\\n<value>    | 4 bytes |
    +---------+----------------+------------+----------------------+---------+

``header_crc`` is the crc32 of the magic and length bytes. It makes a
partial header that borrows bytes from a following frame fail validation,
so an incomplete record in the middle of the log reads as corruption while
a genuinely short final header reads as a torn tail.

Metadata is a compact JSON object: ``{"t":"p","k":key}`` for puts,
``{"t":"d","k":key}`` for deletes and ``{"t":"c","s":seq}`` for commits.
The raw value bytes follow the first newline, so values need no encoding.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
import zlib

__all__ = ["Store", "CorruptLogError", "inject_tear"]


class CorruptLogError(ValueError):
    """The write-ahead log is corrupt, not merely missing a torn tail.

    A single incomplete final record is a normal crash remnant and is
    discarded during recovery. Anything else that fails framing, checksum,
    metadata or commit-sequence validation is corruption; recovery stops
    without applying or removing anything.
    """


LOG_NAME = "wal.log"
_CHECKPOINT_NAME = "wal.ckp"
_MARKER_NAME = "wal.rec"

_MAGIC = b"WAL2"
_PREFIX = 12  # 4 bytes magic + 8 bytes payload length
_HEADER = 16   # prefix + 4 bytes crc32 of the prefix
_TRAILER = 4   # crc32 of the payload
_MAX_PAYLOAD = 1 << 40

_OP_PUT = "p"
_OP_DELETE = "d"
_OP_COMMIT = "c"


def _encode_frame(op: str, value: bytes = b"", key: str | None = None,
                  seq: int | None = None) -> bytes:
    meta: dict[str, object] = {"t": op}
    if key is not None:
        meta["k"] = key
    if seq is not None:
        meta["s"] = seq
    head = json.dumps(meta, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
    payload = head + b"\n" + value
    prefix = _MAGIC + len(payload).to_bytes(8, "big")
    header = prefix + zlib.crc32(prefix).to_bytes(4, "big")
    return header + payload + zlib.crc32(payload).to_bytes(4, "big")


def _iter_frames(f):
    """Scan an open binary log file from position 0.

    For every intact frame yields
    ``("frame", meta, value, start, end)``. Scanning stops with either no
    terminal event (clean EOF), ``("torn", start)`` for a single incomplete
    final frame, or ``("invalid", start)`` for a frame that fails framing,
    header/payload checksum or metadata parsing. With the header checksum a
    partial header that borrows bytes from a following record cannot survive,
    so a short read landing exactly at EOF is reliably the one unfinished
    record a single writer was appending when it died; bytes left beyond such
    a read instead make it corruption.
    """
    f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
    eof = f.tell()
    f.seek(0)
    while True:
        start = f.tell()
        header = f.read(_HEADER)
        if not header:
            return
        if len(header) < _HEADER:
            # Trailing bytes of a frame header are a torn tail only when
            # nothing follows them; a gap anywhere else is corruption.
            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
                   else ("invalid", start))
            return
        if header[:4] != _MAGIC:
            yield "invalid", start
            return
        if int.from_bytes(header[_PREFIX:], "big") != zlib.crc32(
                header[:_PREFIX]):
            yield "invalid", start
            return
        length = int.from_bytes(header[4:_PREFIX], "big")
        if length > _MAX_PAYLOAD:
            yield "invalid", start
            return
        payload = f.read(length)
        checksum = f.read(_TRAILER)
        if len(payload) < length or len(checksum) < _TRAILER:
            # Only the single final record may be incomplete.
            yield (("torn", start) if f.tell() == eof
                   else ("invalid", start))
            return
        if int.from_bytes(checksum, "big") != zlib.crc32(payload):
            yield "invalid", start
            return
        newline = payload.find(b"\n")
        if newline < 0:
            yield "invalid", start
            return
        try:
            meta = json.loads(payload[:newline])
        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
            yield "invalid", start
            return
        if not isinstance(meta, dict) or not isinstance(meta.get("t"), str):
            yield "invalid", start
            return
        yield "frame", meta, payload[newline + 1:], start, f.tell()


def _fsync_dir(path: str) -> None:
    """Fsync a directory so a nearby rename/unlink is durable.

    Windows cannot open directories for fsync and raises ``PermissionError``
    (access denied); directory entries there are made durable by the file's
    own flush-on-rename, so skipping the directory fsync keeps store creation
    working everywhere.
    """
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        return
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        try:
            os.fsync(fd)
        except PermissionError:
            # Some non-Windows mounts reject directory fsync the same way.
            pass
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _write_all(fd: int, data: bytes) -> None:
    view = memoryview(data)
    while view:
        view = view[os.write(fd, view):]


def inject_tear(source, destination, offset):
    """Copy a log cut at exactly ``offset`` bytes, for bytewise verification.

    Produces ``destination`` containing the first ``offset`` bytes of
    ``source`` -- a replica of a process killed precisely when the write had
    reached that byte offset. The source file is never modified. Either path
    argument may be a store directory, in which case its ``wal.log`` is used.

    ``offset`` must satisfy ``0 <= offset <= len(source)``; a negative or
    past-the-end offset raises ``IndexError``. The full-length copy
    (``offset == len(source)``) is the clean control case.

    Verification aid only; the normal write path never calls this.
    """
    if not isinstance(offset, int) or isinstance(offset, bool):
        raise TypeError("offset must be an integer byte offset")

    src = os.path.join(source, LOG_NAME) if os.path.isdir(source) else source
    dst = (os.path.join(destination, LOG_NAME)
           if os.path.isdir(destination) else destination)

    size = os.path.getsize(src)
    if offset < 0 or offset > size:
        raise IndexError(
            f"tear offset {offset} out of range for log of {size} bytes")
    if os.path.abspath(src) == os.path.abspath(dst):
        raise ValueError("tear destination must differ from the source log")

    remaining = offset
    with open(src, "rb") as fsrc, open(dst, "wb") as fdst:
        while remaining:
            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
            if not chunk:  # pragma: no cover - size came from the same file
                raise IndexError("source log shrank while copying")
            fdst.write(chunk)
            remaining -= len(chunk)
        fdst.truncate(offset)
        os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
    return dst


class Store:
    """A single-writer key value store backed by an append-only log.

    ``path`` must be an existing store directory; the log file inside it is
    created on first use. Opening a missing directory raises
    ``FileNotFoundError`` and opening a path that is not a directory raises
    ``OSError``.

    With ``read_only=True`` the store is opened purely for reading. No file
    is ever created or modified, and no lock is taken: any number of
    read-only processes may coexist with the one writer. The reader pins the
    committed snapshot current at open time -- the highest committed prefix
    of ``wal.log`` or of the atomically replaced ``wal.ckp`` sidecar --
    scans it once, and serves every ``get`` from that in-memory index. The
    snapshot is independent of the log's later history, so a read never
    replays the log and cannot block the writer, and uncommitted bytes, a
    half-written commit, a torn record or a half-finished rebuild are never
    visible. ``put``, ``delete``, ``commit`` and ``recover`` are rejected on
    a read-only store; ``stats`` reports the pinned snapshot.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str, read_only: bool = False):
        self._dir = path
        self._path = os.path.join(path, LOG_NAME)
        self._ckp_path = os.path.join(path, _CHECKPOINT_NAME)
        self._marker_path = os.path.join(path, _MARKER_NAME)
        self._read_only = read_only

        # Recovery needs a directory to replay; a missing target is an error
        # at open time, not an implicit create.
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"store directory does not exist: {path!r}")
        if not os.path.isdir(path):
            raise OSError(f"store path is not a directory: {path!r}")

        self._data: dict[str, bytes] = {}
        self._seq = 0
        self._entries = 0
        self._pending = 0
        self._closed = False
        self._corrupt = False
        # Torn records dropped in this recovery epoch; wal.rec carries it
        # across processes until the next commit.
        self._discarded = 0

        if read_only:
            # A read-only open holds no writable fd and never takes a lock;
            # leave the writer fd slot unset for clarity.
            self._fd = -1
            self._open_read_only()
            return

        log_created = not os.path.exists(self._path)
        self._fd = os.open(self._path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND,
                           0o644)
        if log_created:
            os.fsync(self._fd)
            _fsync_dir(path)

        self._converge_on_open()

    # -- log scanning and validation --------------------------------------

    def _read_log(self, path=None):
        frames = []
        terminal = None
        with open(path or self._path, "rb") as f:
            for event in _iter_frames(f):
                if event[0] == "frame":
                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
                else:
                    terminal = event
        return frames, terminal

    @staticmethod
    def _validate(frames, terminal):
        """Validate every frame and the strictly increasing commit sequence.

        Returns ``(committed_end, last_seq)`` -- the byte offset just past
        the last commit marker and its sequence number. An ``"invalid"``
        terminal is corruption and raises ``CorruptLogError``; a ``"torn"``
        terminal is left for the caller, which decides from the durable
        checkpoint whether it is a tail to discard or a gash to restore.
        """
        expected_seq = 1
        last_seq = 0
        committed_end = 0
        for meta, _value, _start, end in frames:
            op = meta.get("t")
            if op in (_OP_PUT, _OP_DELETE):
                key = meta.get("k")
                if not isinstance(key, str) or key == "":
                    raise CorruptLogError(
                        f"invalid frame metadata: {meta!r}")
            elif op == _OP_COMMIT:
                seq = meta.get("s")
                if not isinstance(seq, int) or isinstance(seq, bool):
                    raise CorruptLogError(
                        f"invalid commit marker: {meta!r}")
                if seq != expected_seq:
                    raise CorruptLogError(
                        f"commit sequence {seq} out of order, "
                        f"expected {expected_seq}")
                last_seq = seq
                expected_seq += 1
                committed_end = end
            else:
                raise CorruptLogError(f"unknown frame type: {op!r}")
        if terminal is not None and terminal[0] == "invalid":
            raise CorruptLogError("corrupt log frame")
        return committed_end, last_seq

    @staticmethod
    def _replay(frames) -> tuple[dict[str, bytes], int]:
        state: dict[str, bytes] = {}
        applied = 0
        for meta, value, _start, _end in frames:
            op = meta["t"]
            if op == _OP_COMMIT:
                continue
            if op == _OP_PUT:
                state[meta["k"]] = value
            else:  # _OP_DELETE
                state.pop(meta["k"], None)
            applied += 1
        return state, applied

    # -- crash-convergence sidecars ---------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, length: int) -> None:
        remaining = length
        while remaining:
            chunk = fsrc.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
            if not chunk:
                raise CorruptLogError(
                    "source ended before the committed prefix")
            fdst.write(chunk)
            remaining -= len(chunk)
        fdst.truncate(length)

    def _atomic_file(self, target: str, write) -> None:
        """Replace ``target`` atomically: temp file, fsync, rename, dir fsync."""
        tmp = target + ".tmp"
        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
            write(f)
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, target)
        _fsync_dir(self._dir)

    def _write_checkpoint(self, end: int) -> None:
        """Persist the log prefix ``[0, end)`` as the clean checkpoint."""
        if end <= 0:
            return

        def write(fdst):
            with open(self._path, "rb") as fsrc:
                self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, end)

        self._atomic_file(self._ckp_path, write)

    def _checkpoint_boundary(self) -> int:
        """Commit boundary the durable checkpoint covers; 0 if absent.

        A checkpoint that is torn, unparseable or not exactly one committed
        prefix is corruption of the recovery machinery rather than a discard.
        """
        try:
            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._ckp_path)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return 0
        if not frames:
            # An empty checkpoint covers the empty prefix; anything non-empty
            # that parses to no frames is corruption.
            if os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path) == 0 and terminal is None:
                return 0
            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint is not a clean committed prefix")
        if terminal is not None:
            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint is not a clean committed prefix")
        end, _seq = self._validate(frames, None)
        if end != os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path):
            raise CorruptLogError("checkpoint has bytes past its commit")
        return end

    def _write_marker(self, clean_end: int, discarded: int) -> None:
        payload = json.dumps(
            {"end": clean_end, "discarded": discarded},
            separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")

        def write(f):
            f.write(payload)

        self._atomic_file(self._marker_path, write)

    def _read_marker(self):
        try:
            with open(self._marker_path, "rb") as f:
                raw = f.read()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        try:
            marker = json.loads(raw)
            end = marker["end"]
            discarded = marker["discarded"]
        except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):
            raise CorruptLogError("unparseable recovery marker")
        if (not isinstance(end, int) or isinstance(end, bool) or end < 0
                or discarded not in (0, 1)):
            raise CorruptLogError("invalid recovery marker")
        return end, discarded

    def _remove_marker(self) -> None:
        try:
            os.unlink(self._marker_path)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return
        _fsync_dir(self._dir)

    def _remove_stale_temps(self) -> None:
        for name in (self._path + ".tmp", self._ckp_path + ".tmp",
                     self._marker_path + ".tmp"):
            try:
                os.unlink(name)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass

    def _rebuild_log(self, clean_end: int) -> None:
        """Make the log exactly its clean ``[0, clean_end)`` prefix.

        Kill-safe and idempotent: when a checkpoint covers the prefix the new
        log is fully written and fsynced as a temp file and atomically renamed
        over the old one, so a kill leaves either the old log or the complete
        restored log -- never a half-written file -- and rerunning converges.
        Without a checkpoint but with the committed bytes still at stable
        offsets, a synced truncate drops the tail instead. The empty prefix is
        a truncate to zero.
        """
        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
        if size == clean_end:
            return

        if clean_end == 0:
            os.ftruncate(self._fd, 0)
            os.fsync(self._fd)
            return

        try:
            ckp_size = os.path.getsize(self._ckp_path)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            ckp_size = -1

        if ckp_size < clean_end and size > clean_end:
            # No checkpoint, but the committed bytes survive at stable
            # offsets: drop the dirty tail. Idempotent if killed mid-call.
            try:
                os.fsync(self._fd)
            except OSError:
                pass
            os.ftruncate(self._fd, clean_end)
            os.fsync(self._fd)
            return
        if ckp_size < clean_end:
            raise CorruptLogError(
                "committed prefix is torn and no checkpoint covers it")

        tmp = self._path + ".tmp"
        with open(self._ckp_path, "rb") as fsrc, open(tmp, "wb") as fdst:
            self._copy_prefix(fsrc, fdst, clean_end)
            os.fsync(fdst.fileno())
        # Windows cannot rename over a path held open by the append fd.
        os.close(self._fd)
        try:
            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
            _fsync_dir(self._dir)
        finally:
            self._fd = os.open(
                self._path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
        if os.fstat(self._fd).st_size != clean_end:
            raise CorruptLogError("restore did not converge")

    def _converge(self):
        """Validate and converge the on-disk log to its clean state.

        Returns ``(frames, discarded)`` for the now-clean log. Raises
        ``CorruptLogError`` without changing anything if the log is corrupt.
        Safe to run repeatedly and safe to kill at any point.

        The durable commit boundary is the highest of the validated log
        boundary, the checkpoint boundary and the marker boundary, so it can
        never regress. A log torn inside its committed prefix is rebuilt from
        the checkpoint and ``discarded`` stays 0 (those bytes were committed,
        not an unfinished write); a torn or merely uncommitted tail past the
        boundary is discarded, and the marker freezes that report until the
        next commit even when the kill lands mid-repair.
        """
        self._remove_stale_temps()
        marker = self._read_marker()
        marker_end = -1
        marker_discarded = 0
        if marker is not None:
            marker_end, marker_discarded = marker

        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
        log_end, _log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
        ckp_end = self._checkpoint_boundary()
        size = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size

        target = max(log_end, ckp_end, marker_end)
        # The target bytes must come from somewhere still on disk: the
        # validated log itself or the checkpoint.
        if target > log_end and target > ckp_end:
            raise CorruptLogError("recovery target has no durable source")

        log_clean = terminal is None and size == log_end

        if log_clean and log_end == target:
            # Nothing to repair. An old marker whose epoch a newer commit
            # closed durably can finally go; otherwise its discarded count
            # stays frozen until that commit.
            if marker is not None:
                if target > marker_end:
                    self._remove_marker()
                    discarded = 0
                else:
                    discarded = marker_discarded
            else:
                discarded = 0
            if ckp_end < target:
                self._write_checkpoint(target)
            return frames, discarded

        if target > log_end:
            # Committed bytes were torn away (offset 0 included): the
            # checkpoint is the source of truth. The discarded count is only
            # meaningful when the marker pins this exact boundary.
            discarded = marker_discarded if target == marker_end else 0
            self._rebuild_log(target)
        else:
            # A dirty suffix sits past the boundary. Decide discarded from
            # the suffix itself: a torn final record counts, complete
            # uncommitted frames do not. This also covers a repair killed
            # before the rebuild (the original suffix is still here, so the
            # same decision is reached) and fresh writes appended after a
            # previous repair (a new crash is a new decision rather than the
            # old marker's). A marker is only frozen once the log itself is
            # rebuilt clean; see the clean branch above.
            discarded = 1 if terminal is not None else 0
            if ckp_end < target:
                # Make the prefix independently restorable before we publish
                # the plan or remove any bytes.
                self._write_checkpoint(target)
            self._write_marker(target, discarded)
            self._rebuild_log(target)

        frames, terminal = self._read_log()
        end, _seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
        if end != target or terminal is not None:
            raise CorruptLogError("restore did not converge")
        return frames, discarded

    def _publish(self, frames, discarded) -> None:
        state, _applied = self._replay(frames)
        self._data = state
        self._seq = max(
            (meta["s"] for meta, _v, _s, _e in frames
             if meta.get("t") == _OP_COMMIT),
            default=0)
        self._entries = len(frames)
        self._pending = 0
        self._discarded = discarded
        self._corrupt = False

    def _converge_on_open(self) -> None:
        """Crash cleanup at open; leave a corrupt store inert for recover()."""
        try:
            frames, discarded = self._converge()
        except CorruptLogError:
            self._corrupt = True
            return
        self._publish(frames, discarded)

    # -- read-only opens --------------------------------------------------

    def _open_read_only(self) -> None:
        """Pin a committed snapshot without creating or modifying anything.

        No lock is taken and nothing on disk is written. The reader chooses
        the highest committed prefix available at the instant it opens --
        the validated prefix of ``wal.log`` or the existing ``wal.ckp``
        sidecar, which the writer replaces atomically as part of every
        commit -- scans that prefix once into memory, and serves every
        ``get`` from that index. Later reads are independent of log history,
        never replay the log and never block the writer.

        The checkpoint is a complete, self-contained image that is never
        modified in place (only atomically replaced), so reading it cannot
        expose uncommitted bytes, a half-written commit, a torn record or a
        half-finished rebuild/shrink. It is also what makes the pin safe once
        the reader closes the file: the image survives any later rename.
        """
        frames, end, seq = self._choose_readonly_prefix()
        state, _applied = self._replay(frames)
        self._ro_index: dict[str, bytes] = state
        self._ro_seq = seq
        self._ro_entries = len(frames)
        self._ro_bytes = end

    def _choose_readonly_prefix(self):
        """Return ``(frames, end, seq)`` for the highest committed snapshot.

        Takes the higher of the validated log boundary and the checkpoint
        boundary, mirroring the writer's durable-boundary rule. A torn or
        merely uncommitted tail past the last commit is excluded; a framing
        or sequence failure in committed bytes is corruption and raises
        ``CorruptLogError``. The checkpoint is the source when a crash or a
        concurrent rebuild has torn/shrunk the committed log bytes.
        """
        log_frames = None
        log_end = -1
        log_seq = 0
        if os.path.exists(self._path):
            frames, terminal = self._read_log(self._path)
            log_end, log_seq = self._validate(frames, terminal)
            # Keep only frames at or before the last commit; the torn final
            # record already arrives as the terminal, not as a frame.
            log_frames = [fr for fr in frames if fr[3] <= log_end]

        ckp = self._read_clean_prefix(self._ckp_path)
        if ckp is None:
            if log_frames is None:
                return [], 0, 0
            return log_frames, log_end, log_seq

        ckp_frames, ckp_end, ckp_seq = ckp
        if log_end >= ckp_end:
            return log_frames, log_end, log_seq
        return ckp_frames, ckp_end, ckp_seq

    def _read_clean_prefix(self, path: str):
        """Validate ``path`` as an exact committed prefix.

        Returns ``(frames, end, seq)`` or ``None`` if the file is absent.
        Raises ``CorruptLogError`` when it exists but is not exactly a clean
        committed prefix: such a sidecar is replaced atomically, so a torn
        or unparseable image cannot be a publish caught mid-flight. The size
        used for the "bytes past its commit" check is taken from the same
        open inode that was scanned, so a concurrent atomic replace can
        never mix the bytes of one version with the size of another.
        """
        try:
            f = open(path, "rb")
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        with f:
            frames = []
            terminal = None
            for event in _iter_frames(f):
                if event[0] == "frame":
                    _, meta, value, start, end = event
                    frames.append((meta, value, start, end))
                else:
                    terminal = event
            size = os.fstat(f.fileno()).st_size
        if terminal is not None:
            raise CorruptLogError("sidecar is not a clean committed prefix")
        if not frames:
            if size == 0:
                return frames, 0, 0
            raise CorruptLogError("sidecar is not a clean committed prefix")
        end, seq = self._validate(frames, None)
        if end != size:
            raise CorruptLogError("sidecar has bytes past its commit")
        return frames, end, seq

    def _read_key(self, key: str) -> bytes | None:
        value = self._ro_index.get(key)
        return None if value is None else bytes(value)

    # -- argument validation ----------------------------------------------

    @staticmethod
    def _check_key(key) -> None:
        if not isinstance(key, str):
            raise TypeError("key must be a string")
        if key == "":
            raise ValueError("key must not be empty")

    def _ensure_open(self) -> None:
        if self._closed:
            raise ValueError("store is closed")

    def _ensure_writable(self) -> None:
        self._ensure_open()
        if self._read_only:
            raise ValueError("store is opened read-only")
        if self._corrupt:
            raise CorruptLogError(
                "log is corrupt; call recover() to diagnose before writing")

    # -- public API --------------------------------------------------------

    def put(self, key: str, value: bytes) -> None:
        self._ensure_writable()
        self._check_key(key)
        if not isinstance(value, bytes):
            raise TypeError("value must be bytes")
        _write_all(self._fd, _encode_frame(_OP_PUT, value=value, key=key))
        self._data[key] = value
        self._pending += 1
        self._entries += 1

    def get(self, key: str) -> bytes | None:
        self._ensure_open()
        self._check_key(key)
        if self._read_only:
            return self._read_key(key)
        return self._data.get(key)

    def delete(self, key: str) -> None:
        self._ensure_writable()
        self._check_key(key)
        _write_all(self._fd, _encode_frame(_OP_DELETE, key=key))
        self._data.pop(key, None)
        self._pending += 1
        self._entries += 1

    def commit(self) -> int:
        self._ensure_writable()
        if self._pending == 0:
            return self._seq
        _write_all(self._fd, _encode_frame(_OP_COMMIT, seq=self._seq + 1))
        os.fsync(self._fd)

        # The commit frame is durable first, so even a kill here leaves a
        # clean log the next open refreshes the checkpoint from. Publish the
        # new restorable prefix, then close the recovery epoch.
        clean_end = os.fstat(self._fd).st_size
        self._write_checkpoint(clean_end)
        had_marker = os.path.exists(self._marker_path)
        self._seq += 1
        self._pending = 0
        self._entries += 1
        self._discarded = 0
        if had_marker:
            self._remove_marker()
        return self._seq

    def recover(self) -> dict:
        """Replay the log and return ``{"applied", "discarded", "seq"}``.

        ``applied`` counts the committed put/delete records replayed,
        ``discarded`` is 1 when a single torn final record was dropped (0
        otherwise) and ``seq`` is the durable sequence number after recovery.
        Raises ``CorruptLogError`` (a ``ValueError``) if the log is corrupt;
        nothing is applied or truncated in that case.

        Recovery is idempotent and kill-safe: interrupting it any number of
        times and rerunning converges to the same state and the same report
        as one clean recovery, and the next commit always uses ``seq + 1``.
        """
        self._ensure_open()
        if self._read_only:
            raise ValueError("cannot recover a store opened read-only")
        if self._pending:
            raise ValueError(
                "cannot recover with uncommitted changes in this session")

        # Re-validate and re-converge; a genuinely corrupt log raises here
        # before anything is applied or removed.
        frames, discarded = self._converge()

        state, applied = self._replay(frames)
        seq = max(
            (meta["s"] for meta, _v, _s, _e in frames
             if meta.get("t") == _OP_COMMIT),
            default=0)
        self._data = state
        self._seq = seq
        self._entries = len(frames)
        self._pending = 0
        self._discarded = discarded
        self._corrupt = False
        return {"applied": applied, "discarded": discarded, "seq": seq}

    def stats(self) -> dict:
        self._ensure_open()
        if self._read_only:
            # The pinned snapshot's sequence, frame count and byte size; it
            # does not move as the writer appends later history.
            return {
                "seq": self._ro_seq,
                "entries": self._ro_entries,
                "bytes": self._ro_bytes,
            }
        return {
            "seq": self._seq,
            "entries": self._entries,
            "bytes": os.fstat(self._fd).st_size,
        }

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self._closed:
            return
        if not self._read_only:
            os.close(self._fd)
        self._closed = True

    def __enter__(self) -> "Store":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
        self.close()
